examples.ko: 간접흡연은 아이들 건강에 특히 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Second-hand smoke is especially bad for children's health.
I want to avoid second-hand smoke at restaurants.
I'm worried about second-hand smoke because of my family.

examples.ko: 간접흡연 피해를 줄이려고 환기를 자주 해요.
examples.en: I ventilate often to reduce the harm of second-hand smoke.
Some people cough because of second-hand smoke.
You have to be careful about second-hand smoke at bus stops too.

explain: 내가 피우지 않아도 다른 사람의 연기를 마시게 되는 것을 말하고, 반대말은 '직접흡연'이에요. '간접흡연 피해', '간접흡연에 노출되다'처럼 건강 이야기나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 발음은 [간저프변]으로 소리 나요.
explain_en: It describes breathing in someone else's smoke even though you don't smoke yourself, and its opposite is '직접흡연' (direct smoking). It often appears in health talk and news in phrases like '간접흡연 피해' and '간접흡연에 노출되다'. It is pronounced [간저프변].

examples.ko: 구제역 때문에 소를 키우는 농가가 힘들어요.
examples.en: Farms that raise cattle are struggling because of foot-and-mouth disease.
The news says foot-and-mouth disease has spread.
When it breaks out, they block entry to farms.
The government supports vaccination against foot-and-mouth disease.

examples.ko: 지난겨울에 구제역이 돌아서 고기 값이 올랐어요.
examples.en: Foot-and-mouth disease went around last winter, so meat prices rose.
The village where it was found stayed quiet for a while.

explain: 소, 돼지 같은 동물이 걸리는 병이라서 사람의 병에는 쓰지 않아요. 뉴스에서는 '구제역이 발생하다', '구제역이 확산되다', '구제역 방역'처럼 써요. 새가 걸리는 병은 '조류인플루엔자'라고 해서 달라요.
explain_en: It is a disease of animals such as cattle and pigs, never of people. In the news: '구제역이 발생하다', '구제역이 확산되다', and '구제역 방역'. A disease in birds is '조류인플루엔자', a different term.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 당뇨가 있어서 단 음식을 조심해요.
examples.en: My grandfather has diabetes, so he is careful with sweet food.
Steady management is important for diabetes.
I also had a diabetes test at my health checkup.
My father takes diabetes medicine every day.
I started exercising to prevent diabetes.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 당뇨 때문에 설탕을 줄이라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to cut down on sugar because of diabetes.

explain: 병원에서는 '당뇨병'이라고 하고, 일상에서는 줄여서 '당뇨'라고 많이 해요. '당뇨가 있다'라고 말하고, 병에 걸렸다고 할 때는 '당뇨병에 걸리다'가 자연스러워요. 피 속의 당은 '혈당'이라고 해요.
explain_en: At the hospital the full word is 당뇨병, but in daily life people shorten it to 당뇨. You say 당뇨가 있다, and for catching the disease the natural phrase is 당뇨병에 걸리다. Sugar in the blood is called 혈당.

examples.ko: 갑자기 딸꾹질이 나서 말을 못 하겠어요.
examples.en: I suddenly got the hiccups and can't speak.

examples.ko: 물을 마시면 딸꾹질이 멈출 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes drinking water stops the hiccups.
I ate too fast, so I'm hiccuping.
The baby hiccuped for a long time, so I was worried.
They say hiccups stop if you get a fright.
The hiccups started right before my presentation, and I panicked.

explain: '딸꾹질이 나다'가 가장 자연스럽고, 멈출 때는 '멎다'나 '멈추다'를 써요. '딸꾹'은 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 놀라면 멎는다는 말이 한국에서 흔해요.
explain_en: 딸꾹질이 나다 is the most natural phrase, and it stops with 멎다 or 멈추다. 딸꾹 imitates the sound. A common Korean belief is that a scare makes hiccups stop.

examples.en: There are many bacteria on your hands.
Bacteria cannot be seen with the eye.
I wash my hands with soap to get rid of bacteria.
The food was contaminated with bacteria.
Cheese and yogurt are sometimes made using bacteria.
There are bacteria that are good for the body too.

explain: '세균'이라는 한자어도 같은 대상을 가리켜요. 유산균처럼 몸에 좋은 박테리아도 있어서, 나쁜 것만 말할 때는 '병균'이라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: The Sino-Korean word '세균' points to the same thing. Some bacteria, like lactic acid bacteria, are good for the body, and the harmful ones are separately called '병균'.

examples.en: As soon as I got on the boat, I got terribly seasick.
I took seasickness medicine and boarded the boat.
Seasickness gets worse the higher the waves are.

examples.ko: 저는 뱃멀미 때문에 제주도 갈 때 비행기를 타요.
examples.en: Because of seasickness, I take a plane when I go to Jeju.
To reduce seasickness, look into the distance.
I suffered from seasickness and couldn't even eat lunch.

explain: 배를 탔을 때 생기는 멀미예요. 그냥 '멀미'라고도 하지만, 배에서 생긴 것임을 분명히 할 때 뱃멀미라고 해요. 차에서는 '차멀미'라고 해요.
explain_en: This is the motion sickness you get on a boat. You can also just say '멀미', but 뱃멀미 makes it clear it happened on a boat. For cars, the word is '차멀미'.

examples.en: This garment shrinks a lot when washed.
When it's cold, blood vessels contract.

examples.ko: 근육 수축 때문에 다리에 쥐가 났어요.
examples.en: I got a cramp in my leg because of muscle contraction.
I'm worried about the market contracting because of the bad economy.
The doctor explained how the heart contracts and relaxes.

examples.ko: 세탁 뒤에 수축 정도를 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Please check how much it shrinks after washing.

explain: 수축은 부피나 크기가 작아지는 일이에요. 몸의 근육이나 혈관, 옷감이 줄어드는 것, 경제가 위축되는 것에 두루 써요. 반대말은 '팽창'이고 근육에서는 '이완'과 짝으로 나와요.
explain_en: 수축 is the process of becoming smaller in volume or size. It covers muscles, blood vessels, fabric shrinking, and also an economy contracting. Its opposite is '팽창', and for muscles it pairs with '이완' (relaxation).

examples.en: My grandfather goes to the hospital because of heart disease.
Heart disease is easier to treat when found early.

examples.ko: 가족 중에 심장병이 있는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Someone in my family has heart disease.
Exercise helps if you want to prevent heart disease.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 심장병에 좋은 음식을 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me about foods that are good for heart disease.
I visited a friend who was hospitalized for heart disease.

explain: '심장이 안 좋다'는 가볍게도 쓰는 말이지만 '심장병'은 병 이름이에요. '위장병', '피부병'처럼 몸의 부분 이름 뒤에 '병'을 붙여요.
explain_en: Saying '심장이 안 좋다' can be casual, but 심장병 is the name of an illness. Disease names are often formed by adding 병 after a body part, as in 위장병 and 피부병.

examples.en: I stood up suddenly and felt dizzy, so I sat down.
If the dizziness continues, go see a doctor.
I feel dizzy every morning, so I'm worried.
I get severe dizziness when I ride a boat.
I left work early today because of dizziness.
After taking medicine, the dizziness calmed down a lot.

explain: '어지럽다'에서 나온 말이에요. 말할 때는 '어지러워요'라고 하는 경우가 많고, 병원에서 증상을 설명하거나 글로 쓸 때 '어지럼증'이 자주 나와요. '어지럼증이 나다/생기다/있다'와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It comes from '어지럽다' (to be dizzy). In speech people often just say '어지러워요', while '어지럼증' appears often when describing symptoms at a hospital or in writing. It goes well with '어지럼증이 나다/생기다/있다'.

en: to be hot; to be pungent

examples.en: My eardrums tingled for a moment from the shout.
I ate spicy tteokbokki, and my tongue is burning and numb.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 귀가 얼얼해요.
examples.en: I was outside on a cold day, and my ears are stinging.

examples.ko: 세게 부딪혀서 이마가 얼얼해서 한참 문질렀어요.
examples.en: I bumped my forehead hard, and it stung, so I rubbed it for a while.
The malatang is so numbingly hot, but it's delicious.

examples.ko: 얼얼하던 손이 따뜻한 물에 담그니 풀렸어요.
examples.en: My numb, stinging hand loosened up when I soaked it in warm water.

explain: 매운 음식, 추위, 부딪친 아픔 때문에 그 부분이 따끔하고 감각이 무뎌진 느낌이에요. 맛에는 '얼얼한 맛'처럼 매워서 혀가 마비되는 듯한 느낌을 말하고, 그냥 '맵다'보다 감각이 둔해지는 느낌이 더해져요.
explain_en: It describes a part of the body feeling stinging and dulled from spicy food, cold or a knock. For taste, '얼얼한 맛' means a spiciness that makes the tongue feel numb, adding a dulled sensation to plain '맵다' (spicy).

examples.ko: 한여름에 오래 밖에 있으면 열사병에 걸릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you stay outside for long in midsummer, you can get heatstroke.

examples.ko: 열사병을 예방하려면 물을 자주 마셔야 해요.
examples.en: To prevent heatstroke, you should drink water often.
A student collapsed from heatstroke on the field.

examples.ko: 열사병은 위험하니까 빨리 병원에 가야 해요.
examples.en: Heatstroke is dangerous, so you must go to the hospital quickly.
If heatstroke symptoms appear, move to the shade.
If you suspect heatstroke, call 119 right away.

explain: 더운 곳에서 체온이 너무 올라 생기는 위험한 병이에요. 가볍게는 '더위를 먹다'라고 말하는데, 어지럽고 기운이 없는 정도를 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is a dangerous condition where body temperature rises too high in hot conditions. For milder cases people say '더위를 먹다', meaning feeling dizzy and drained from the heat.

examples.en: I have the chills, so maybe I caught a cold.

examples.ko: 열이 오르기 전에 심한 오한을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: I felt a severe chill before my fever rose.

examples.ko: 오한 때문에 이불을 두 겹이나 덮었어요.
examples.en: Because of the chills, I covered myself with two layers of blankets.

examples.ko: 몸살이 나면 오한과 근육통이 같이 와요.
examples.en: When you come down with body aches, chills and muscle pain come together.
If the chills continue, please go to the hospital.

examples.ko: 갑자기 오한이 들어서 일찍 집에 왔어요.
examples.en: I suddenly got the chills, so I came home early.

explain: 몸이 아플 때 으슬으슬 춥고 떨리는 느낌이에요. 보통 '오한이 나다', '오한이 들다'로 써요. 무서워서 소름 돋는 느낌은 '오싹하다'라고 하고, 이 말과 달라요.
explain_en: It is the shivery, cold feeling when your body is ill. It is usually used as '오한이 나다' or '오한이 들다'. The goosebump feeling from fear is '오싹하다', which is different.

examples.ko: 더운 날 밖에서 오래 놀다가 일사병에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: I got sunstroke from playing outside too long on a hot day.

examples.ko: 일사병을 막으려면 모자를 쓰고 물을 자주 마시세요.
examples.en: To prevent sunstroke, wear a hat and drink water often.
There was a student who collapsed from sunstroke on the field.

examples.ko: 일사병 증상이 있으면 그늘에서 쉬어야 해요.
examples.en: If you have symptoms of sunstroke, you should rest in the shade.

examples.ko: 뙤약볕 아래서 일하면 일사병이 생기기 쉬워요.
examples.en: Working under the scorching sun makes sunstroke easy to get.
You have to watch out for sunstroke at summer festivals.

explain: 강한 햇볕을 오래 받아서 생기는 병이에요. 비슷한 '열사병'은 몸의 열이 너무 올라가 더 위험할 때 말해요. 일상에서는 '더위를 먹다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: This is the illness caused by long exposure to strong sunlight. The similar '열사병' refers to the body overheating, which is more dangerous. In daily talk people often say '더위를 먹다' as well.

examples.en: I fell and scraped my knee.
Luckily I only got a light scrape.
I put a bandage on the wound because of the scrape.
It was a bike accident and I got a graze on my arm.

examples.ko: 찰과상은 먼저 깨끗한 물로 씻어 주세요.
examples.en: First wash a scrape with clean water.

examples.ko: 아이가 놀이터에서 놀다가 찰과상을 입고 울었어요.
examples.en: The child scraped herself while playing at the playground and cried.

explain: 스치거나 쓸려서 피부 겉이 벗겨진 얕은 상처예요. 뉴스나 병원에서는 '찰과상'이라고 하고, 일상에서는 '무릎이 까졌어요'처럼 말해요. '찰과상을 입다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is a shallow wound where the skin surface is scraped off. In the news and at the hospital people say '찰과상', while in daily life they say things like '무릎이 까졌어요'. A common phrase is '찰과상을 입다'.

examples.en: I got caught in the rain, and my clothes are soaked and damp.

examples.ko: 땀에 젖은 머리카락이 이마에 축축이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: My sweaty hair is clinging damply to my forehead.
Tears dampened my cheeks.
I wet a towel well and wiped my face.
The ground is wet and damp, so be careful.
Dew has gathered damply on the blades of grass.

explain: '축축하다'의 부사형으로, 물기가 배어서 눅눅하게 젖은 모양을 말해요. '촉촉이'는 알맞게 부드럽게 젖은 좋은 느낌이 많고, 축축이는 불쾌하게 젖은 느낌에 자주 써요.
explain_en: It's the adverb of '축축하다', describing something soaked through and clammy. '촉촉이' often feels pleasant and gently moist, while 축축이 is often used for an unpleasantly damp feeling.

examples.en: My grandfather was diagnosed with lung cancer.
Lung cancer is easier to treat if found early.
The doctor said it was not lung cancer.

examples.ko: 폐암을 예방하려면 검진을 받는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: To prevent lung cancer, it's good to get screened.
My neighbor who suffered from lung cancer recovered.
Lung cancer can also be found in a health checkup.

explain: '폐'는 몸속 장기 이름이고 '암'은 병 이름이에요. '위암', '간암'처럼 장기 이름 뒤에 '암'을 붙여서 '폐암 환자', '폐암 검사'라고 써요.
explain_en: 폐 is the lung and 암 is cancer. Like 위암 and 간암, you attach 암 after the organ name, as in 폐암 환자 or 폐암 검사.

examples.en: These days I feel very tired all day.

examples.ko: 오래 운전한 날은 피로감을 많이 느껴요.
examples.en: On days I drive for a long time, I feel very fatigued.
After taking medicine, the fatigue eased a little.

examples.ko: 피로감 때문에 회의 내내 집중하기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: Because of the fatigue, it was hard to concentrate during the whole meeting.
With body aches and fatigue on top, I took a day off.
I'm suffering from fatigue and feel sleepy even during the day.

explain: '피로'는 몸이 지친 상태 자체이고, '피로감'은 그렇게 느끼는 기분이에요. 그래서 '피로감을 느끼다', '피로감이 쌓이다'처럼 말해요. 일상에서는 '피곤하다'를 훨씬 편하게 써요.
explain_en: '피로' is the state of being worn out, and '피로감' is the feeling of it, so we say '피로감을 느끼다' or '피로감이 쌓이다'. In everyday speech, '피곤하다' is the more casual choice.

examples.ko: 장마철에 비가 계속 오면 피부병이 늘어요.
examples.en: When it keeps raining in the monsoon season, skin diseases increase.
The puppy caught a skin disease, so we went to the vet.

examples.ko: 피부병은 손으로 긁으면 더 심해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: A skin disease can get worse if you scratch it.

examples.ko: 피부병 약을 하루에 두 번 발라요.
examples.en: I apply the skin medicine twice a day.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 피부병 치료는 꾸준히 해야 한다고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said skin disease treatment must be kept up steadily.

examples.ko: 홍수 뒤에는 피부병과 감기가 돌기 쉬워요.
examples.en: After a flood, skin diseases and colds easily spread.

explain: '피부병에 걸리다'처럼 '걸리다'와 함께 써요. 가벼운 문제는 '피부 트러블'이라고 많이 말하고, '피부병'은 병원에서 치료가 필요한 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '걸리다', as in '피부병에 걸리다'. For minor problems people often say '피부 트러블', while '피부병' sounds more like something that needs medical treatment.
